Variants.Content: Legitimacy is the public reason why a person or family is qualified to rule. It may come from blood, appointment, conquest, custom, or recognition. Nobles invoked it to win vassals, and commoners often only felt whether it stood up when taxes, trials, and armies arrived.

Entry Dynastic Legitimacy Legitimacy is the public reason why a person or family is qualified to rule. It may come from blood, appointment, conquest, custom, or recognition. Nobles invoked it to win vassals, and commoners often only felt whether it stood up when taxes, trials, and armies arrived. Whether it is valid depends on who can grant the rights, collect the consideration, and actually make the judgment come to fruition in the event of default.

The distant system is not empty talk only if it can be implemented in campfires, city gates and inns.

If a rule is practiced over and over again, it will find its way into rituals, crafts, and prayers; if it is sustained only by fear, cracks will show at the onset of a crisis.
